title: Flap-Flap! Yankel's Shoe
summary: On Tu BiShvat everyone dances around the little tree with baskets of dried fruit, and little Yankel jumps the highest... until his old shoe tears and goes flap-flap! Yankel stands to the side, barefoot and sad, but Adele, a kind woman with a shoe shop, runs to bring him new shoes: one too big, one too small, and one just right. When Yankel goes back to dancing, he blesses her that her home will have joy and a little baby. A rhyming story based on a tale from Shivchei HaBesht, retold for Tu BiShvat.
pages:
Tu BiShvat! The garden is full of light,
they dance round the tree like a ball, round and bright.
Baskets in hand, and a date on each one,
and little Yankel jumps in the circle, what fun!

Yankel's shoes are old, so very, very old,
patch on a patch, and more patches, all told!
But Yankel doesn't worry, he sings and he laughs all day,
and he jumps like a child who is out at play.

Higher and higher, he jumps to the treetop, whoo!
And suddenly — rrrip! — oh no, a tear in his shoe!
The sole popped open like a fox's mouth, through and through:
Flap-flap, flap-flap! goes the shoe.

Yankel tied it with string, but the string slipped away,
he hopped on one foot like a stork — and fell, crash, in the clay!
He tiptoed slowly, the way a camel would do:
Flap-flap, flap-flap! goes the shoe.

Yankel took off the shoe and stood to the side,
barefoot and sad, with no dancing, alone, while he sighed.
Everyone's in the circle, singing and clapping their hands,
and Yankel just watches, with a tear, where he stands.

By the gate stood Adele, with a heart warm and wide,
and she saw it all, all of it, from her side.
And Adele has a shop, and in the shop, guess what's there?
Shoes! Shelf after shelf, all new, pair after pair!

Adele ran to her shop and hurried back too,
with a giant shoe, like a boat with no hole coming through.
Yankel stepped in, and it was big as a basket, it's true:
Flap-flap, flap-flap! goes the shoe.

So she brought a small shoe, like one for an elf,
Yankel pushed and he pushed, and his toe peeked out like a mouse from a shelf!
Then a third shoe, not too big and not too tight...
Just right! And Yankel shouted: "Hooray! Hurrah! What a sight!"

Yankel went back to the circle and jumped high as a tower, whoo-hoo!
Tap-tap, tap-tap! goes the shoe.
Then he stopped by Adele and said with a smile big and true:
"May there be a baby in your home, and joy, and songs, and everything, too!"

Tu BiShvat! Again the garden is full of light,
again they dance round the tree like a ball, round and bright.
And up on Yankel's shoulders, bouncing in the circle, look who:
it's Adele's baby! Tap-tap! goes the shoe.
